availableCommands.name: copy-request-id
availableCommands.description: Copy the last request ID to clipboard

availableCommands.name: multi-model-review
availableCommands.description: Pick models (structured question or inline), then parallel Task reviewers (global)

availableCommands.name: simplify
availableCommands.description: Find low-info comments, one-off helpers, perf issues, and reuse opportunities. (global)

availableCommands.name: agent-sdk-create-agent
availableCommands.description: Scaffold a new Agent SDK agent: short AskQuestion interview, then verify a turn and hand off to hillclimb. Use to build or create a new bot or agent with the agent-sdk, the Agent SDK, `@grok/agent-sdk`, or BDK. Ask only what the invoking message left open. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: autopilot
availableCommands.description: Keep a PR merge-ready by triaging comments, resolving clear conflicts, and fixing CI in a loop. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: create-hook
availableCommands.description: Create Cursor hooks. Use when you want to create a hook, write hooks.json, add hook scripts, or automate behavior around agent events. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: create-rule
availableCommands.description: Create Cursor rules for persistent AI guidance. Use when you want to create a rule, add coding standards, set up project conventions, configure file-specific patterns, create RULE.md files, or asks about .cursor/rules/ or AGENTS.md. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: create-skill
availableCommands.description: Create Cursor Agent Skills. Use when authoring a new skill or asking about SKILL.md structure. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: create-subagent
availableCommands.description: Create custom subagents for specialized AI tasks. Use when you want to create a new type of subagent, set up task-specific agents, configure code reviewers, debuggers, or domain-specific assistants with custom prompts. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: goal
availableCommands.description: Set a goal that Cursor will pursue to completion. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: loop
availableCommands.description: Run a prompt or skill in this session on a recurring or variable interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: migrate-to-skills
availableCommands.description: Convert 'Applied intelligently' Cursor rules (.cursor/rules/*.mdc) and slash commands (.cursor/commands/*.md) to Agent Skills format (.cursor/skills/). Use when you want to migrate rules or commands to skills, convert .mdc rules to SKILL.md format, or consolidate commands into the skills directory. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: new-repo
availableCommands.description: Create a Cursor-hosted repo for the current project and push it. Use when a project has no git remote yet and the user asks to create a repo on Cursor, push the project to Cursor, or set up a Cursor-hosted remote; installs and signs in the origin CLI when needed. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: origin
availableCommands.description: Install, sign in, update, or repair the origin CLI for repos hosted on Cursor (origin.cursor.com). Use when the CLI is missing or outdated, git push/pull fails to authenticate against origin.cursor.com, or the user asks to set up, clone, or configure Cursor-hosted repos. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: rename-chat
availableCommands.description: Rename the current chat to match its focus. Use only when the user invokes /rename-chat. Optional text after the command steers the title. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: sdk
availableCommands.description: Guide users building apps, scripts, CI pipelines, or automations on top of the Cursor SDK - TypeScript (`@cursor/sdk`) or Python (`cursor-sdk` / `cursor_sdk`). Use when the user mentions integrating, installing, or writing code against the Cursor SDK; says `Agent.create`, `Agent.prompt`, `Agent.resume`, `agent.send`, `agent.summarize`, `run.stream`, `run.messages`, `SDKSummaryMessage`, `CursorAgentError`, `@cursor/sdk`, `cursor-sdk`, or `cursor_sdk`; asks to run Cursor agents programmatically from a script, CI/CD pipeline, GitHub Action, backend service, or other code outside the Cursor IDE; wants to pick between local and cloud runtime, configure MCP servers for an SDK agent, handle streaming, cancellation, or errors, or keep a long conversation within the context window; or is wiring Cursor into an automation, bot, or REST `/v1/agents` migration. Use eagerly rather than answering from memory; the SDK surface evolves and this skill is the source of truth for the external packages. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: share
availableCommands.description: Save, back up, or share the current project on Cursor — creates a repo (a saved, versioned copy that isn't public) even for users who have never used git, handling all setup automatically. Use when the user asks to save, back up, publish, or share their project on Cursor, or how to not lose it. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: shell
availableCommands.description: Runs the rest of a /shell request as a literal shell command. Use only when the user explicitly invokes /shell and wants the following text executed directly in the terminal. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: split-to-prs
availableCommands.description: Split current work into small reviewable PRs. Use when the user asks to split a chat, set of changes, branch, or PR. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: statusline
availableCommands.description: Configure a custom status line in the CLI. Use when the user mentions status line, statusline, statusLine, CLI status bar, prompt footer customization, or wants to add session context above the prompt. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: update-cli-config
availableCommands.description: View and modify Cursor CLI configuration settings in ~/.cursor/cli-config.json. Use when the user wants to change CLI settings, configure permissions, switch approval mode, enable vim mode, toggle display options, configure sandbox, or manage any CLI preferences. (builtin skill)

availableCommands.name: ask-matt
availableCommands.description: Ask which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the skills in this repo. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: chief-of-staff
availableCommands.description: Pursue a long-running goal in a single session by co-ordinating subagents. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: claude-handoff
availableCommands.description: Hand the current conversation off to a fresh background agent that picks up the work immediately. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: code-review
availableCommands.description: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X". (user skill)

availableCommands.name: codebase-design
availableCommands.description: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: diagnosing-bugs
availableCommands.description: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: domain-modeling
availableCommands.description: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a GLOSSARY.md, or recording or editing an ADR. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: find-skills
availableCommands.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: git-guardrails-claude-code
availableCommands.description: Set up Claude Code hooks to block dangerous git commands (push, reset --hard, clean, branch -D, etc.) before they execute. Use when user wants to prevent destructive git operations, add git safety hooks, or block git push/reset in Claude Code. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: grill-me
availableCommands.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: grill-with-docs
availableCommands.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design, which also creates docs (ADR's and glossary) as we go. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: grilling
availableCommands.description: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: handoff
availableCommands.description: Compact the current conversation into a handoff document for another agent to pick up. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: implement-spec
availableCommands.description: Implement the result of /to-spec and /to-tickets in code. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: implement
availableCommands.description: Implement a piece of work based on a spec or set of tickets. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: improve-codebase-architecture
availableCommands.description: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: loop-me
availableCommands.description: Grill me about specs for the workflows I want to build, within this workspace. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: migrate-to-shoehorn
availableCommands.description: Migrate test files from `as` type assertions to @total-typescript/shoehorn. Use when user mentions shoehorn, wants to replace `as` in tests, or needs partial test data. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: pr
availableCommands.description: Use when writing a PR body. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: prototype
availableCommands.description: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: research
availableCommands.description: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: retro
availableCommands.description: Conduct a retrospective on a coding session. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: scaffold-exercises
availableCommands.description: Create exercise directory structures with sections, problems, solutions, and explainers that pass linting. Use when user wants to scaffold exercises, create exercise stubs, or set up a new course section. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: setup-matt-pocock-skills
availableCommands.description: Configure this repo for the engineering skills: set up its issue tracker, triage label vocabulary, and domain doc layout. Run once before first use of the other engineering skills. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: setup-pre-commit
availableCommands.description: Set up Husky pre-commit hooks with lint-staged (Prettier), type checking, and tests in the current repo. Use when user wants to add pre-commit hooks, set up Husky, configure lint-staged, or add commit-time formatting/typechecking/testing. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: setup-ts-deep-modules
availableCommands.description: Wire dependency-cruiser into a TypeScript repo so each package is a deep module, with implementation hidden in subfolders and reachable only through its entry-point files. User-invoked. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: tdd
availableCommands.description: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: teach
availableCommands.description: Teach the user a new skill or concept, within this workspace. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: to-questionnaire
availableCommands.description: Turn a decision you can't fully answer into a questionnaire for someone else to fill in. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: to-spec
availableCommands.description: Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the project issue tracker: no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: to-tickets
availableCommands.description: Break a plan, spec, or the current conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, published to the configured tracker (edges as text in one file per ticket locally, or native blocking links on a real tracker). (user skill)

availableCommands.name: triage
availableCommands.description: Move issues and external PRs through a state machine of triage roles, categorise, verify, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: wait-what
availableCommands.description: Stop. That last message did not land: re-pitch it. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: wayfinder
availableCommands.description: Plan a huge chunk of work (more than one agent session can hold) as a shared map of decision tickets on your issue tracker, and resolve them one at a time until the way to the destination is clear. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: wizard
availableCommands.description: Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform. Use when provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: writing-beats
availableCommands.description: Writing, exploit; assemble raw material into a journey of beats, grounding each term before a beat leans on it. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: writing-for-agents
availableCommands.description: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: writing-fragments
availableCommands.description: Writing, explore: mine raw fragments, no structure yet. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: writing-shape
availableCommands.description: Writing, exploit: shape raw material into an article, paragraph by paragraph. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: frontend-design
availableCommands.description: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: teach

availableCommands.name: to-questionnaire
availableCommands.description: Turn a decision you can't fully answer into a questionnaire for someone else to fill in. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: to-spec
availableCommands.description: Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the project issue tracker: no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: to-tickets
availableCommands.description: Break a plan, spec, or the current conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, published to the configured tracker (edges as text in one file per ticket locally, or native blocking links on a real tracker). (user skill)

availableCommands.name: triage
availableCommands.description: Move issues and external PRs through a state machine of triage roles, categorise, verify, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: wait-what
availableCommands.description: Stop. That last message did not land: re-pitch it. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: wayfinder
availableCommands.description: Plan a huge chunk of work (more than one agent session can hold) as a shared map of decision tickets on your issue tracker, and resolve them one at a time until the way to the destination is clear. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: wizard
availableCommands.description: Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform. Use when provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: writing-for-agents
availableCommands.description: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: writing-fragments
availableCommands.description: Writing, explore: mine raw fragments, no structure yet. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: writing-shape
availableCommands.description: Writing, exploit: shape raw material into an article, paragraph by paragraph. (user skill)

availableCommands.name: frontend-design
